case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns Bluetooth qualification planning for a product using Nordic-based modules, Bluetooth Mesh, GATT, beacon functionality, and Multi-Design qualification reuse. The customer seeks guidance on qualification scope, reusable QDIDs, SDK version alignment, module substitution, membership requirements, qualification timing, and qualification fees. The discussion evolves from initial qualification planning through qualification strategy selection and finally proceeds toward registration support and qualification fee payment. The final outcome is a Multi-Design qualification approach using existing qualified designs and customer-managed qualification fee payment.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical discussion focuses on how to qualify a product that combines a prequalified module, Nordic software components, and Bluetooth Mesh functionality. The consultant explains that qualification eligibility depends on the exact qualified designs, SDK versions, SoftDevice versions, and Mesh subsystem versions implemented in the product. The thread clarifies that Mesh functionality and standard GATT/beacon functionality may require separate referenced qualified components rather than relying solely on a Mesh subsystem qualification. It also explains when module substitutions, antenna variations, sensor changes, SDK changes, or future feature additions do or do not require new qualification activity. Additional discussion covers Multi-Design reuse, membership requirements, specification version determination from referenced designs, and obtaining a 16-bit UUID.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Qualification decisions are driven by the specific qualified designs actually referenced by the product implementation. The implemented SDK versions, SoftDevice versions, Mesh components, and module qualifications must match the referenced qualification records. Specification version, qualification scope, and reuse eligibility are determined by the referenced qualified designs rather than marketing claims, module datasheets, or desired target versions. Where multiple qualified components are required to cover product functionality, a Multi-Design declaration must be used.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using SDK versions or software components that do not correspond to available qualified designs can invalidate the planned qualification strategy and require redesign or requalification. Misidentifying reusable QDIDs, assuming module substitutions are always covered, or referencing incorrect qualification records can result in declaration errors and qualification delays. Failing to align implemented software versions with referenced qualification records can create qualification inconsistencies requiring additional review or qualification work. Delaying membership, qualification fee payment, or registration preparation can jeopardize the desired qualification schedule.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: An incorrect QDID reference was provided during the discussion and was later corrected after the customer could not locate the referenced qualification in Qualification Search. The correction clarified the proper qualified design reference and reinforced the need to verify exact QDID identifiers before providing qualification guidance.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Bluetooth qualification reuse is only valid when the product implementation precisely matches the qualified modules, software components, SDK versions, and qualified designs being referenced. Always validate the exact qualification records, software versions, and Multi-Design composition before committing to a qualification strategy.
